I am an old man here in Iringa, farming this land my family has held for many years. The rains here are usually good, so I do not need to bring water from anywhere — God sends the rain for my maize. I have no money for the chemical fertilizer from the shop, it is too expensive, but I keep some cattle and goats so I spread their manure on the plot before planting. I use the seed I saved from last year's harvest like my father taught me, and I intercrop with beans to help the soil and feed my family.
